key_impacts: Nuclear fuel melted inside reactors (core meltdown).
Contaminated coolant water leaked into reactor building basements.
Around 400 tons of groundwater flowed into the site daily, worsening contamination management.
Large numbers of 1,000‑ton tanks used to store contaminated water on site, with stability concerns.
Ongoing cooling required to prevent further releases of radioactive materials.
evidence_snippets: Large-scale nuclear disaster at TEPCO’s Fukushima Daiichi… directly caused by the Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami of March 11, 2011.
Coolant water is circulated to cool the nuclear fuel that melted inside the nuclear reactors due to the accident.
It becomes extremely contaminated and leaks into the basement… 400 tons of groundwater are flowing in everyday… site has been packed with 1,000 ton capacity tanks.
missing_information: Impact figures for casualties/evacuations not provided in the excerpt.
